subject: Private deployment keystore handover and DPA clarifications
messages:
From: Emily Rogers <emily@medicahealth.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jonathan Price <jonathan.price@procureco.com>
Date: 2025-08-24 09:12 -0700
Subject: Questions on keystore custody + DPA for private deployment

Hi Camila,

Thanks for yesterday's demo — team appreciated the overview of the VPC/private deployment option. We're moving this through procurement and security and have a few items we need clarified before we can sign the DPA + SOW: 

1) Key custody model: We want explicit language that MedicaHealth will retain exclusive control of the customer-managed key (CMK) used for data-at-rest encryption. What processes will Redwood follow for emergency operator access or break-glass scenarios?

2) Operator access boundaries: Please outline what telemetry and metadata Redwood will collect from the private deployment control plane vs. what remains in our VPC.

3) Subprocessor disclosure: We need a list of subprocessors that will have any network-level access to the tenant environment (e.g., monitoring, backups).

I'm attaching a short questionnaire from security and a draft SOW itemizing the keystore handover. Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept the DPA redline about customer key ownership, and whether you can provide an escrow/contact for local key recovery?

Goal: finalize DPA/SOW this week so procurement can issue PO.

Cheers,
Emily Rogers
VP Information Security
MedicaHealth

Attachments: Medica_DPA_Questions.pdf, Proposed_Handover_SOW.docx

From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emily Rogers <emily@medicahealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>; Neha Kapoor <neha@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2025-08-24 11:03 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on keystore custody + DPA for private deployment

Hi Emily — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Laura (sales lead on this account) and Neha (product/security PM) so we can get concrete answers. Quick summary up front: Redwood supports BYOK for private deployments, and customers retain exclusive control of CMKs. We'll provide an operator handover playbook and an escrow option; details below.

Answers (high-level):
- Key custody: Customer retains exclusive ownership and control. Redwood can be provisioned as a "guardian" only in a documented break-glass procedure that requires 3-party authorization (Customer Sec lead + Redwood Security lead + Legal). We recommend the break-glass flow be codified in the SOW annex.
- Operator access/telemetry: The private control plane will collect aggregated routing/health metrics (pgp-hashed instance ids, call latencies) but no unredacted request payloads. Customer telemetry endpoints remain in the VPC and logs under your retention policy unless you opt-in to export a subset to Redwood for support.
- Subprocessors: We'll provide a short, dated list in the next message; primary subprocessors for this deployment are cloud provider managed services in the customer's region (if you choose Redwood-managed infra), and our support vendor for incident diagnostics if you grant explicit network access.

I've attached a proposed keystore-access matrix and marked the fields we'd like to negotiate in the SOW. Neha — can you confirm the technical mechanics for a break-glass escrow and what minimal telemetry is strictly required for support?

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: keystore-access-matrix.csv

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emily Rogers <emily@medicahealth.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwoodinference.com>; Laura Bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2025-08-24 14:20 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on keystore custody + DPA for private deployment

Emily — thanks for sharing the questionnaire. Below are technical specifics we can include in the DPA/SOW annex: 

1) BYOK mechanics: The customer supplies the CMK via a secure upload into your keystore (we support AWS KMS-interoperable wrapping or raw PKCS#11 import for on-prem HSM). The CMK never leaves your control plane. Redwood maintains only a hashed binding and a policy token; we cannot decrypt keys.

2) Break-glass / operator recovery: We offer two options: (A) Customer-managed escrow: you deposit an encrypted recovery blob with a named escrow agent (customer-chosen) and Redwood documents the recovery protocol; or (B) Redwood-assisted recovery: executed only under the 3-party authorization and with a full audit trail plus short-lived ephemeral credentials that expire immediately after the action. All operator actions are recorded in the control plane audit log and customers can request forensic exports.

3) Minimal telemetry: Required support telemetry includes instance health (CPU, memory), per-route handshake latencies, and error traces (no request payloads). Optional telemetry exports (only if you opt-in) include anonymized token counts and aggregated model selection metrics for cost tuning.

4) Subprocessor disclosure: We will provide a dated list in the contract (annex B). For MedicaHealth specifically, the only potential subprocessors with network access would be: (i) Managed infra partner in us-east-1 (if chosen), (ii) our diagnostics partner for packet captures during approved incident windows — only with explicit consent.

I'll prepare an SOW annex and a short redline-friendly clause you can insert into your DPA.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Product Security Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachment: (see keystore-access-matrix.csv)

2) We need the final, dated subprocessor table to land in Annex B — please include names, purpose, and last-verified date.

Date: 2025-08-26 16:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on keystore custody + DPA for private deployment

Team — attaching the redline-ready DPA snippet and an SOW annex that includes: explicit CMK ownership language, the two escrow options with step-by-step break-glass flow, an SLA target for operator-assisted actions (max 8 business hours to complete recovery under the 3-party flow), and the initial dated subprocessor table.

Highlights of the annex: 
- "Customer retains sole control and ownership of CMKs used to encrypt customer data; Redwood will not possess unencrypted key material."
- Break-glass requires written approval from Customer Sec lead and Redwood Security lead; any emergency action is recorded and audit bundle delivered within 24 hours.
- Subprocessor table (Annex B) enumerates the managed infra partner and diagnostics vendor; any additional subprocessors will require 30-day notice.

Next steps: Please confirm you received these attachments and we'll coordinate a short call (30 min) tomorrow to sign off. If procurement is ready, Camila — happy to accept a PO reference after legal confirms the redlines.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
